5. CONFOUNDERS: This is a single-arm Phase 2 trial (n=30 evaluable) with no randomized comparator, which limits causal inference. The lack of a control arm means we cannot rule out natural disease fluctuation or selection bias. The small sample size limits generalizability. SAEs were present (hypokalemia 10%, intracranial hemorrhage 3.3%, elevated troponin 3.3%) but did not appear to prevent adequate dosing or drive trial termination. The trial ran its full planned duration of ~5 years follow-up. These are real design caveats but do not negate the positive outcome signal.

review_reason: Single-arm trial with no randomized comparator and no biomarker/PD data. The 90% 5-year OS is clinically impressive for severe/refractory SLE but cannot be definitively attributed to the treatment mechanism without a control arm. Historical OS benchmarks for this population are needed to contextualize the effect size. Additionally, the trial reports OS as the primary endpoint for a transplant procedure in an autoimmune disease, which is an unusual endpoint choice (disease activity/remission endpoints are more typical for SLE); expert review is warranted to assess whether OS adequately captures the treatment benefit in this indication.
